tg-subj-i-ga.erklaerung: In Korean, 이/가 marks the subject of a sentence — the person or thing doing the action or being described. Attach 가 after a noun ending in a vowel, and 이 after a noun ending in a consonant. For example: 친구가 와요 (my friend is coming) or 학생이 있어요 (there is a student). This particle basically points at 'who or what' the sentence is about. Native English speakers often skip it because English doesn't need a subject marker, but in Korean it's essential to show who/what is doing something, especially when the subject isn't obvious from context. The most common mistake is using 는/은 instead of 이/가, or forgetting the particle entirely — 이/가 introduces new or specific information (often 'what', 'who', or something happening right now), while 는/은 tends to set up contrast or topic. Just remember: check the last letter of the noun — vowel gets 가, consonant gets 이!

beispiele.tr: A student is in the classroom.

tg-subj-i-ga.produzieren: Write two sentences about your daily life using 이/가 to mark the subject — for example, talk about your friend, family member, or the weather today.
